newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebel chief says offensive delayed for talks.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebel chief says offensive delayed for talks.

text.p: Zaire rebel leader Laurent Kabila said rebels delayed an offensive as a sign of goodwill during talks in South Africa but he would only negotiate on the issue of President Mobutu Sese Seko relinquishing power.

Kabila told Reuters in the eastern Zairean city of Bukavu late on Friday a ceasefire was not yet an issue in the talks and if there was no progress rebels would fight on to force Kinshasa to negotiate.

"We have temporarily stopped our intention of launching our counter-offensive during this time of negotiations (in South Africa) as a sign of goodwill," Kabila said. "We're willing to sustain this goodwill for a few days.
"But if there is no advance on this question of negotiations we will be forced to launch our offensive...It's very important for us to push those people (Zaire) to the negotiating table."

Asked with whom he would be willing to negotiate from the Zairean government side, the rebel chief said: "Anyone who has in their hands the power to make important decisions. For us the only issue to be negotiated is the stepping down of Mobutu."
